verdict_text:
YES

The script verifies the key sets match and that every non-MLP tensor is bit-identical across all three checkpoints before any modification, aborting via assertion otherwise. It then computes each of the 64 MLP tensors in float32 as `base + 0.4*(ft1-base) + 0.4*(ft2-base)` against the unmodified base, casts back to the base dtype, and takes all other tensors from the base unchanged with the same names. It asserts exactly 64 tensors were merged and 244 are in the output, and writes a single file to `out/T4/model.safetensors`. The duplicate `import json` is harmless.
